payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery in which the dopant suppresses electrolyte crossover and associated aging. Independent auditing corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge. The cell’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, with a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. It cannot operate below 4 °C because the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte.

payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce negative-electrolyte crossover, a major aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. An independent teardown audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, retracting the earlier 12,000-cycle claim because it used un-normalized depth of discharge. The audit confirmed gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg and an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop. A conference assessment projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale.
